stem:
Meera keeps a steel tiffin box on her study table. She notices that the tiffin box always keeps the same shape and the same size, no matter where she places it.

Why does a solid like the steel tiffin box have a definite shape and a definite volume?

options.text: Its particles are tightly packed and attract each other very strongly, so they stay in fixed positions and only vibrate.
Its particles are tightly packed, and this tight packing alone holds the shape even though the particles attract each other only weakly.
Its particles move freely throughout the box but the hard outer surface stops the box from changing shape.
The fixed shape and volume of the box push its particles close together and make their attractions strong.

teacher.key_rationale: A solid keeps a definite shape and volume because its particles are tightly packed AND the interparticle attractions are very strong, holding particles in fixed positions where they only vibrate. Both conditions are needed. Option B drops the strong-attraction condition, making tight packing alone seem sufficient (condition_omission trap). Option C wrongly invokes free particle movement and an external surface. Option D reverses cause and effect.
